record.paper_title: On chromatic numbers of space-times: open problems
record.original_question: Suppose a system-changing process takes proper time 1 in Minkowski space-time. What is the smallest number of states needed so that whenever two objects coincide at the same space-time point they are always in the same state, under the requirement induced by a unit proper-time transition?

evidence.quote: An alternative, more physical meaning: let us assume that some system-changing process takes a proper time τ0 – hence, in the appropriate measuring units, the proper time 1.
What is the smallest number of states for which the two objects at the same point in space-time are always in the same state?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Minkowski space-time $\mathbb{R}^{1,d}$ (for some fixed spatial dimension $d \ge 1$) equipped with the pseudo-Euclidean form
$$Q(x-y) = (x_0 - y_0)^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{d}(x_i - y_i)^2.$$
Define the graph $G$ whose vertex set is $\mathbb{R}^{1,d}$ and in which two points $x,y$ are adjacent if and only if $Q(x-y) = 1$ (i.e., they are separated by unit proper time along some time-like geodesic). 

Determine the chromatic number $\chi(G)$, that is, the smallest cardinal $k$ such that there exists a map $c:\mathbb{R}^{1,d}\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ with $c(x)\neq c(y)$ whenever $Q(x-y)=1$. Equivalently: what is the smallest number of "states" that must be assigned to space-time points so that any two points connected by a unit-proper-time transition receive different states?
artifact.status_search_result: The exact chromatic number of Minkowski space-time with the unit proper-time relation appears to remain open, as the pseudo-Euclidean analogue of the Hadwiger–Nelson problem. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:2308.16885) establishes related finiteness/Ramsey-type statements such as: every finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}^2$ contains a monochromatic pair $(x,y),(x',y')$ with $(x-x')^2-(y-y')^2=1$, but does not pin down the precise chromatic number. The Hadwiger–Nelson problem itself (Euclidean analogue) is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Chromatic number of spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: Answers a problem of Kosheleva and Kreinovich on a pseudo-Euclidean analogue of the Hadwiger-Nelson problem; shows every finite colouring of Q^2 contains a monochromatic pair with (x-x')^2-(y-y')^2=1; a density version in Z^2 remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The chromatic-number-of-spacetime question is an active analogue of Hadwiger–Nelson with related questions still open.

status_evidence.title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The chromatic number of the plane satisfies 5 ≤ χ(R^2) ≤ 7; exact value unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The Euclidean analogue of the problem is itself open, supporting that the Minkowski version is open.
